summary: This note is a long, compiled Wikipedia-style overview of the State of Israel. It covers its location and borders, climate, economy and water technology, and its population and languages. It also traces the country's history from ancient Judah and the Balfour Declaration through the 1947 UN Partition Plan, later peace agreements, and recent foreign relations and defense spending.
one_line: Wikipedia-derived overview of Israel's geography, climate, economy, population, languages, transport, and history from ancient times to the present.
key_facts: On 11 March 1978, a PLO guerilla raid from Lebanon led to the Coastal Road Massacre.
Israel's financial and technology center is Tel Aviv, while Jerusalem is the self-designated capital and most populous individual city under the country's governmental administration.
Israeli sovereignty over Jerusalem is internationally unrecognized.
The highest temperature in the continent of Asia (54.0 °C or 129.2 °F) was recorded in 1942 at Tirat Zvi kibbutz in the northern Jordan river valley.
On 29 November 1947, the General Assembly adopted Resolution 181 (II) recommending the adoption and implementation of the Plan of Partition with Economic Union.
The population of Israel, as defined by the Israel Central Bureau of Statistics, was estimated in 2016 to be 8,476,600 people, with 74.9% designated as Jewish.
Israel is the world's only Jewish-majority state.
The Israel–Jordan Treaty of Peace was signed in 1994, making Jordan the second Arab country to normalize relations with Israel.
While leaving a peace rally in November 1995, Yitzhak Rabin was assassinated by a far-right-wing Jew who opposed the Accords.
The Merneptah Stele of ancient Egypt, dated to the late 13th century BCE, is the earliest known archaeological artifact to mention the word "Israel".
By 2014, Israel's desalination programs provided roughly 35% of Israel's drinking water, and it is expected to supply 40% by 2015 and 70% by 2050.
In 2013, a record of 3.54 million tourists visited Israel, with 68% of tourists visiting the Western Wall.
In 1984, Israel spent 24% of its GDP on defense; by 2006 that figure had dropped to 7.3%.
The sovereign territory of Israel is approximately 20,770 square kilometers (8,019 sq mi) in area, of which two percent is water.
